Indian Standard ( Reaffirmed 2005 ) 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

METAL BONE SCREWS — MECHANICAL 

REQUIREMENTS AND METHODS OF TEST 

PART i SCREWS WITH ASYMMETRICAL THREAD, VARIABLE 
FITTING (SPHERICAL), STAINLESS STEEL 



1. Scope — Specifies the characteristics of, and corresponding mechanical test methods for metal 
bone screws used in surgery. 

2. Material — Bone screws conforming to this specification shall be manufactured from stainless 
steel, composition B, in accordance with IS : 5347-1969 ' General requirements of metal surgical 
hnplants*. 

3. Dimensions — Each of the screws in the test sample shall conform to the dimensional 
requirements specified in IS : 9829 (Part I )-1981 'Specification for metal bone screws: P^rtiScrews 
with asymmetric thread, variable fitting (spherical). 

4- Mechanical Properties — Each of the screws in the test sample shall be tested for the minimum 
breaking torque and the minimum angle of rotation to failure (see 7). The minimum breaking 
torque and minimum angle of rotation to failure shall be as specified in Table 1.

5. Surface Finish— -The surface of metal bone screws shall be free, when examined with the 
naked eye, of imperfections, such as nicks, scratches and other defects that would impair the 
serviceability of the screw. The final finish shall be continuous and free, when examined with 
the naked eye, of marks which are the results of previous operations such as grinding, polishing, 
burnishing, tumbling, etc, 

6. Compliance and Retests — Should any of the screws in the test sample not comply with any 
of the requirements, a further sample, comprising at least twice the number of screws of the 
original test sample, shall be taken from the lot in question and all tested as described above. Any 
failure amongst the second sample of screws shall constitute failure of the particular lot of screws 
to comply with this standard. 

7. Determination of Breaking Torque and Angle of Rotation at Failure 

7.1 Test Equipment — The testing equipment shall satisfy the following: 

a) The maximum sensitivity on the lowest measuring range is not to be less than O'OI N.m or 
its equivalent, and on other scales not less than 1 percent of full range deflection. 

b) Selection of loading scale range, see 7.2.4. 

c) The measuring device shall be capable of registering and indicating the reading of the 
maximum torque attained during the test.

d) Unless the device, through which the torque is applied to the screw head, is capable of 
being clamped to prevent movement in the vertical direction, a device to prevent ' cam out* 
of the driver from the screw head should be incorporated Into the system. 

e) The screw shall b^ clamped in such a manner as to prevent movement of the clamped 
portion of the screw ^nd to ensure correct alignment, 

7.2 Procedure 

7.2-1 Insert the screw under test in the test block so that five full threads from the thread run-oat 
are exposed. If less than five full threads are available, the results shall be accompanied by a 
statement of the precise test conditions. 

7-2.2 Apply torque at a uniform rotational frequency within the range 1 to 5 r/min. 

7.2.3 Load until fracture occurs and record the maximum torsional moment and the angle of 
rotation at failure. 

7.2.4 Should the maximum torque recorded be less than 20 percent of the full range deflection 
of the scale, the test shall be repeated at a lower scale range. 

7.3 Test Report — The test report shall include the following particulars: 

a) Reference to this Indian Standard; 

b) Maximum torsional moment, expressed to the nearest OM N.m and given as the ' breaking 
torque '. 

c) Angle of rotation at failure, expressed to the nearest 10"^ . 

d) A statement of the precise test conditions if less than five full threads are exposed 
(see 7.2.1 ). 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

This standard is based on ISO 6475/1-1980 (E) Implants for surgery-metal bone screws — 
Mechanical reqifirement and method of tests — Part I: Screws with asymmetrical thread, variable 
fitting (spherlcaOr stainless steel, issued by the International Organization for Standardization 
(ISO).
